text: {"translation": "The second quarter of 2026 reported an increase of 1% in net sales. This increase was mainly due to an increase in sales volume in the T&HS segment and a favorable impact of currency exchange in F&II - South America, but was partially offset by a decline in price mix and sales volume in F&II - US and Canada. Excluding the impact of currency exchange, the net sales for the second quarter decreased by 26% year-over-year. The reported operating income and adjusted operating income for the second quarter were $18,800 million (approximately 297 billion yen) and $25,800 million (approximately 407 billion yen), respectively. The difference between the reported operating income and the adjusted operating income was mainly due to impairment expenses, costs associated with the closure of the Cabo factory in Brazil, and costs related to a heat-related incident at the Algo factory that was previously reported. Excluding the impact of currency exchange, the reported operating income decreased by 32% year-over-year, and the adjusted operating income decreased by 7% year-over-year. The operating income of the Textures & Health Solutions segment for the second quarter was $11,700 million (approximately 185 billion yen), an increase of $90 million (approximately 1.4 billion yen) year-over-year. This increase was mainly due to an increase in sales volume, but was partially offset by unfavorable price mix and an increase in tapioca raw material costs. Excluding the impact of currency exchange, the operating income of the segment increased by 5% year-over-year. The operating income of the Food & Industrial Raw Materials - South America segment for the second quarter was $11,800 million (approximately 186 billion yen), a decrease of $90 million (approximately 1.4 billion yen) year-over-year. This decrease was mainly due to the impact of the trading currency in Mexico and a tough demand environment. Excluding the impact of currency exchange, the operating income of the segment decreased by 10% year-over-year. The operating income of the Food & Industrial Raw Materials - US and Canada segment for the second quarter was $5,800 million (approximately 91 billion yen), a decrease of $2,800 million (approximately 4.4 billion yen) year-over-year. This decrease was mainly due to a decline in production at the Algo factory that had normalized by the end of the quarter, a decrease in sales volume, and an unfavorable price mix. Excluding the impact of currency exchange, the operating income of the segment decreased by 33% year-over-year. The operating income of the 'All Other' segment for the second quarter was $76 million (approximately 1.1 billion yen), an increase of $700 million (approximately 11 billion yen) year-over-year. The 'All Other' segment includes multiple business segments that are not individually or collectively classified as reporting segments. The net sales of the 'All Other' segment are mainly from the sale of sweeteners and starches from the Pakistan business, the sale of stevia and other raw materials from the PureCircle business and other sugar reduction businesses, and the sale of endou bean protein raw materials from the protein fortification business. As of June 30, 2026, the total debt was $180 million (approximately 283.9 billion yen), and the cash including short-term investments was $952 million (approximately 150.2 billion yen). As of December 31, 2025, the total debt was $180 million (approximately 283.9 billion yen), and the cash was $1 billion (approximately 157.7 billion yen). The capital expenditures for the second quarter of 2026 were $210 million (approximately 33.1 billion yen). The capital expenditures for the second quarter of 2025 were $12 million (approximately 1.9 billion yen). This was mainly due to derivatives used to hedge the pound exposure related to the planned acquisition of Tate & Lyle, and a foreign exchange gain of $47 million (approximately 74 billion yen) due to the revaluation. The reported effective tax rate and the adjusted effective tax rate for the second quarter were 33.7% and 27.2%, respectively (the reported effective tax rate and the adjusted effective tax rate for the second quarter of 2025 were 23.6% and 27.2%, respectively). The increase in the reported effective tax rate was mainly due to the sale of a majority stake in the Pakistan business and the fluctuation of the Mexican peso to the US dollar. These impacts were partially offset by the utilization of unused capital losses. As of June 30, 2026, the total capital expenditures were $210 million (approximately 33.1 billion yen)."}
